Source: [`docs/specs/features/001-mvp/specs/0005-playout-timeline.md`](../specs/features/001-mvp/specs/0005-playout-timeline.md)

This plan delivers the derived playout timeline and channel state.
kraziBrain decides which playout item is current, the join offset, and which
items follow. The server reads every contributing row from one
connection-pinned schedule snapshot and exposes `GET /channels/:id/now` and
`GET /channels/:id/playout`. It closes what plan 0004 handed here: the
torn-read snapshot integration test, `media_unavailable`, and
channel-state-triggered coverage (SCH-011). Plan 0006 SIG-012 then maps this
plan's `PlayoutService` into the signal `PlayoutProvider` and
`ChannelAuthorization` ports, and SIG-013 keeps the SQLite
`TransitionCoordinator` (see Hand-off).

## Delivery Strategy

Work proceeds in five bands:

1. Policy: record the resolved decisions in spec 0005 and move snapshot
   ownership out of plan 0006 SIG-012 before any code exists.
2. Deterministic core: pure current-state, following-item, and timeline
   derivation in `packages/krazi-brain`, driven test-first.
3. Snapshot: the playout queries and the connection-pinned snapshot read in
   `apps/server`, then the two-connection torn-read proof.
4. API: `PlayoutService` with its single coverage retry, then the `/now` and
   `/playout` routes.
5. Acceptance: drive every criterion over HTTP and hand off.

Every ticket leaves the repository green. Its verification always includes the
`AGENTS.md` **Before You Finish** checks; tickets do not repeat them. Tests use
temporary SQLite databases, Fastify injection, and the plan 0002 to 0004
helpers. Concurrency tests coordinate with barriers and hooks, never sleeps.

## Architecture and Ownership

```text
apps/server
  playout/             playout queries, snapshot read, PlayoutService, /now and /playout
  schedules/           ensureCoverage is the only write step; gains one pure helper
  channels/runtime/    SIG-012 maps PlayoutService into the signal ports (plan 0006)
        |
        `---- packages/krazi-brain/src/playout/
                 pure derivation: playable media, current item, join offset,
                 next and following items, window timeline (no DB, no signal)
```

- `packages/krazi-brain/src/playout/` owns every playout decision: what media
  is playable, which entry covers an instant, the join offset, which
  item is next, the contiguous following prefix, and which entries a window
  timeline contains. It takes plain typed inputs, returns plain results, owns
  its own types, and stays dependency-free. It never imports `packages/signal`.
- `apps/server/src/playout/` owns the playout queries, the snapshot read, the
  coverage retry, evaluation time, error mapping, HTTP validation, and response
  shapes.
- `PlayoutService` issues no SQL writes itself; coverage writes go through
  `ScheduleService.ensureCoverage` between two snapshots.
- Kysely row shapes and transaction objects never cross into kraziBrain or
  `packages/signal`. SIG-012 converts kraziBrain results into signal port
  types inside `apps/server`.

## Resolved Implementation Policies

- **Playable media.** A media item is playable when its status is `available`,
  its `durationMs` is a positive safe integer, and `hasAudio` is not null. The
  catalog check constraint already guarantees the last two for `available`
  rows; kraziBrain checks all three anyway so a bad projection can never reach
  packaging. Playable is deliberately separate from schedulable: it has no
  duration floor and requires the audio fact packaging needs.
- **Durations.** A playout item's `durationMs` is the media's playable length,
  read from `media_items.duration_ms` in the same snapshot. Airtime is
  `endsAt - startsAt`, copied into the entry at generation. The two differ when
  a rescan changes a file after its entry was published.
- **Evaluation time.** `evaluatedAt` is `at ?? now()`, fixed once per request
  and unchanged by the retry. It is never clamped.
- **Join offset.** `offsetMs = evaluatedAt - startsAt + startOffsetMs`.
  `startOffsetMs` is `0` for every MVP item, so the offset is never negative.
  All arithmetic is integer milliseconds. There is no clamp: media longer than
  its airtime plays from the computed offset, and an offset at or past
  `durationMs` leaves nothing to play, so it is reported as
  `media_unavailable` (see Current item). `/now` and the stream route
  therefore always agree.
- **Current item.** The entry with `startsAt <= evaluatedAt < endsAt`. No such
  entry gives `no_current` with reason `schedule_gap`. A covering entry whose
  media is not playable, or whose `offsetMs >= durationMs` because the media
  was re-probed shorter than its airtime, gives `no_current` with reason
  `media_unavailable` and its `scheduleEntryId`. The schedule is never changed
  and no other program is substituted.
- **Early media end.** A following item whose media is shorter than its
  airtime is still selected; SIG-012 limits its `playDurationMs` to the media
  length. What the session transmits for the remaining airtime is a signal
  concern, outside spec 0005.
- **Unplayable boundary.** When the entry after the current one is unplayable,
  the following prefix is empty and the worker fails at the boundary. Tunes
  then get `media_unavailable` until that entry ends. The MVP accepts this;
  filler is the future replacement policy.
- **Next item.** The entry immediately after the current one in sequence order,
  but only when it starts exactly at the current item's `endsAt` and its media
  is playable. Otherwise `nextItem` is `null`, as it always is with no current
  item. Near the edge of coverage the next entry may not be generated yet,
  which also gives `null`.
- **Following items.** `getFollowing(channelId, afterScheduleEntryId, count)`
  returns `stale_entry` when the cursor entry no longer exists on the channel,
  because regeneration deleted it. Otherwise it walks entries after the cursor
  in sequence order and returns the prefix that is contiguous by time
  (`next.startsAt === previous.endsAt`, starting from the cursor's `endsAt`)
  and playable, stopping at the first gap, unplayable item, or `count` items.
  An empty selection is valid. Contiguity is by time, never by
  `sequenceNumber + 1`, because sequence numbers are not reused after
  regeneration; sequence order stays a server query concern.
- **Window timeline.** `GET /channels/:id/playout` returns playable entries
  overlapping `[start, end)` as playout items. Unplayable entries are omitted;
  `/now` is where `media_unavailable` is reported.
- **Missing state.** A channel with no `channel_schedule_states` row reports
  `scheduleRevision: 0`. Revisions start at `1`, so `0` never collides with a
  real revision. Playout responses use `0` where `GET /channels/:id/schedule`
  uses `null`, because the signal ports require a number.
- **Snapshot read.** `readPlayoutSnapshot` opens one ordinary
  `db.transaction()`. It reads `loadScheduleState` first, which fixes the
  SQLite read snapshot, then the channel row, then the playout rows, all
  through the same `trx`. Its database parameter is typed
  `Pick<Kysely<DatabaseSchema>, "transaction">` and its `read` callback
  receives only `trx`, so snapshot code cannot compile a root-handle query.
  Kysely holds one connection mutex per instance, so a root query inside the
  callback would hang rather than read another snapshot. The snapshot never
  writes and is never upgraded.
- **Coverage decision.** The first snapshot computes
  `target = resolveTarget(effectiveNow, through)`, where
  `effectiveNow = max(now(), state.updatedAt)` comes from a new pure
  `effectiveNow` helper in `schedule-coverage.ts` that `clampToLastMutation`
  also uses. It reports `coverage_needed` with that `target` when
  `checkCoverage(state, target)` says a chunk is needed. `through` is `at` for
  `/now` and absent otherwise. A target past `SCHEDULE_REQUEST_LIMIT_MS`
  reports `through_out_of_range`.
- **Retry.** `PlayoutService` runs: snapshot; on `coverage_needed`,
  `ensureCoverage(channelId, log, through)`; then exactly one more snapshot that
  checks `state.lastGeneratedThrough >= target` against the first snapshot's
  `target` instead of recomputing it. The ensure's own effective time is never
  earlier, so any `covered` outcome satisfies the second check unless another
  writer intervenes. The ensure outcomes map as:

  | `ensureCoverage` outcome | Then                                                                        |
  | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `covered`                | Second snapshot requiring `target`; still short gives `unavailable`         |
  | `unschedulable`          | Second snapshot without a coverage requirement, serving what already exists |
  | `disabled`               | `disabled`                                                                  |
  | `channel_not_found`      | `not_found`                                                                 |
  | `through_out_of_range`   | `through_out_of_range`                                                      |

  `WriteAuthorityBusyError` from the ensure propagates to the shared handler.

- **Disabled channels.** `/now` and `/playout` on a disabled channel return
  `409 channel_disabled`: a disabled channel transmits nothing, so it has no
  channel state. This differs on purpose from `GET /channels/:id/schedule`,
  which still serves a disabled channel's guide.
- **Unschedulable channels.** A channel with no block or no schedulable media
  still answers from whatever entries exist. With none, `/now` returns
  `schedule_gap` and `/playout` returns `200` with no items, unlike
  `/schedule`'s `409 channel_unschedulable`: playout reports what the channel
  transmits, and an empty transmission is a state, not an error.
- **`/now` shape.** `GET /channels/:id/now?at=` takes an optional UTC ISO
  instant; production callers omit it. A future `at` ensures coverage through
  it, so a debug read may extend the horizon; generation is deterministic, so
  this changes when entries are written, never what airs. The response is
  `{ channelId, scheduleRevision, evaluatedAt, currentItem, nextItem }`. Items
  carry `type`, `scheduleEntryId`, `mediaItemId`, `title`, `startsAt`,
  `endsAt`, `durationMs`, `startOffsetMs`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt`;
  `currentItem` also carries `offsetMs`. The no-current variant has
  `currentItem: null`, `nextItem: null`, `reason`, and, for
  `media_unavailable`, `scheduleEntryId`. `mediaPath` and `hasAudio` are
  internal and never serialized. Instants use `toApiTimestamp`.
- **`/playout` shape.** `GET /channels/:id/playout?start&end` shares the
  schedule route's window validation (`start < end`, at most 7 days) and, like
  `/schedule`, ensures coverage without a `through`, so any valid window is
  accepted. It returns `{ channelId, scheduleRevision, items }`, items ordered
  by `startsAt`.
- **Error codes**, all existing, in the existing envelope:

  | Code                | Status | When                                                                   |
  | ------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `channel_not_found` | 404    | Unknown channel                                                        |
  | `channel_disabled`  | 409    | Disabled channel                                                       |
  | `invalid_request`   | 400    | Bad `at`, `start`, or `end`; a window over 7 days; `at` past the limit |
  | `schedule_busy`     | 503    | Write authority busy, or coverage still short after the retry          |

  `schedule_busy` details carry `retryable: true` in both cases. The
  out-of-range message names `at`, not `through`. No new `ApiErrorCode` is
  added.

## Phase 2: Deterministic Core

### PLY-002: Derive current channel state in kraziBrain

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-03. kraziBrain's `playout/` domain derives current
channel state with `deriveChannelState`, and `toPlayoutItem` maps playable
entries for PLY-003 to reuse.

**Goal**

Given a revision, an evaluation instant, and the covering entry with its
successor, return the current item, join offset, and next item, or an
explicit no-current reason.

**Scope**

- `playout/contracts.ts`: input `PlayoutEntry` (entry ID, media item ID,
  title, `startsAt`, `endsAt`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, and
  `media: PlayoutMedia`); `PlayoutMedia` (`path`, `durationMs`, `hasAudio`,
  `status`, nullable as stored); output `PlayoutItem` (the spec's fields plus
  `hasAudio`, `type: "program"`); and `ChannelState` as a `current` /
  `no_current` union.
- `playout/playout-item.ts`: `isPlayableMedia` and `toPlayoutItem`.
- `playout/channel-state.ts`: `deriveChannelState({ channelId,
scheduleRevision, evaluatedAt, entries })`.
- `testing/playout-entries.ts`: a `PlayoutEntry` builder with playable
  defaults, following `schedule-media.ts`.
- Export what `apps/server` needs from `src/index.ts`.

**Out of scope**

- Following items and window timelines (PLY-003).
- Any persistence.

**Blocking dependencies**

- PLY-001.

**Implementation notes**

- `entries` is ordered by sequence and holds at most the covering entry and
  its successor; the function picks the entry covering `evaluatedAt` itself
  and stays correct for any ordered input.
- Write the tests first (`tdd` skill).

**Verification**

- Joining at `20:31:15` an item that started at `20:22:00` gives
  `offsetMs: 555000`, matching the spec example.
- At exactly `startsAt` the offset is `0`; at exactly `endsAt` the entry is
  not current and its successor is.
- An offset one millisecond short of a shortened `durationMs` is current; an
  offset equal to or past it gives `media_unavailable` with the entry's ID;
  media longer than its airtime plays from the unclamped offset.
- No covering entry gives `schedule_gap`. Media that is `missing`,
  `probe_failed`, null-duration, or null-audio gives `media_unavailable` with
  the entry's ID.
- A successor that starts later than `endsAt`, is unplayable, or is absent
  gives `nextItem: null`; a no-current result always has `nextItem: null`.
- Identical inputs give deep-equal results, pinned by a golden case.

**Docs impact**

- None.

### PLY-003: Select following items and window timelines in kraziBrain

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-03. `selectFollowingPlayout` returns the `FollowingPlayout`
union, and `buildPlayoutTimeline` takes `{ channelId, scheduleRevision,
entries }`, because every playout item carries both.

**Goal**

Give workers the contiguous playable items after a cursor, and give the API
the playout items in a bounded window.

**Scope**

- `playout/following-playout.ts`: `selectFollowingPlayout({ channelId,
scheduleRevision, cursor, candidates, count })`, returning `selected` with
  items, or `stale_entry` when `cursor` is undefined.
- `playout/playout-item.ts`: `buildPlayoutTimeline(entries)`, mapping playable
  entries to playout items in order.
- Export both from `src/index.ts`.

**Out of scope**

- Persistence and HTTP.

**Blocking dependencies**

- PLY-002.

**Implementation notes**

- Contiguity starts from `cursor.endsAt` and compares each candidate's
  `startsAt` to the previous item's `endsAt`; never compare sequence numbers.
- `count` is a positive integer; reject anything else as a programming error.

**Verification**

- Three contiguous playable candidates with `count: 2` return the first two.
- A time gap, an unplayable candidate, or a candidate not starting at the
  cursor's end stops the selection; a first-candidate stop returns an empty
  `selected`.
- A missing cursor returns `stale_entry` with no items.
- The timeline omits unplayable entries and keeps order.

**Docs impact**

- None.

## Phase 3: Snapshot

### PLY-004: Add the playout queries and the connection-pinned snapshot read

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-03. `playout-repository.ts` holds the four joined
queries; `findPlayoutEntryById` returns a `SequencedPlayoutEntry` so the
following query continues from the cursor's sequence number without kraziBrain
seeing it. `readPlayoutSnapshot` takes a `horizon`, `target`, or `none`
coverage requirement and runs three statements plus the caller's reads.

**Goal**

Read the revision, channel, entries, and media for one result inside one
deferred read transaction, and return a kraziBrain projection or a typed retry
condition, never writing.

**Scope**

- `playout/playout-repository.ts`: executor-agnostic queries joining
  `schedule_entries` and `media_items` into `PlayoutEntry`: the covering entry
  plus its successor at an instant; one entry by ID within the channel; up to
  `count` entries after a sequence number; and entries overlapping a window.
- `playout/contracts.ts`: the snapshot result union `not_found`, `disabled`,
  `coverage_needed` (with `target`), `through_out_of_range`, and `ok` carrying
  the read's value and the revision; and the snapshot options (coverage
  `through`, a required `target` for the retry, no requirement at all, and an
  `afterRevisionRead` test hook).
- `playout/playout-snapshot.ts`: `readPlayoutSnapshot(db, channelId, now,
options, read)` opens `db.transaction()`, runs `loadScheduleState`, then the
  hook, then the channel row, then the coverage decision, then
  `read(trx, revision)`.
- `schedules/schedule-coverage.ts`: extract the pure
  `effectiveNow(now, lastMutation)` and use it from `clampToLastMutation`.
- `GLOSSARY.md`: add **Schedule snapshot**.

**Out of scope**

- The coverage retry and HTTP (PLY-006).

**Blocking dependencies**

- PLY-002.

**Implementation notes**

- The queries use inner joins: `schedule_entries.media_item_id` is a non-null
  foreign key and production never deletes media items, so every entry has a
  media row.
- The queries take any executor so SIG-013 can run the covering query inside
  `runImmediateTransaction`; only `readPlayoutSnapshot` is restricted to
  `transaction`.
- The hook is an injectable option, like `ScheduleService`'s
  `transactionHooks`, and runs after the revision read so a test can pause the
  reader inside its snapshot. The writer's `afterBegin` alone cannot pause the
  reader.

**Verification**

- Enabled, disabled, unknown, and no-state channels return their kinds; a
  no-state channel reports revision `0`.
- A channel short of its horizon returns `coverage_needed` with the target;
  the same channel with no requirement returns `ok`; a supplied `target` the
  state already reaches returns `ok`.
- An `at` past the request limit returns `through_out_of_range`.
- Each query returns the expected entries in sequence order, including a
  missing-status media row and the cursor-not-found case.
- One snapshot runs a bounded, fixed number of statements (`countQueries`).
- `effectiveNow` and `clampToLastMutation` tests stay green.

**Docs impact**

- Add **Schedule snapshot** to `GLOSSARY.md`: a connection-pinned deferred read
  that reads `scheduleRevision` first and every other row through the same
  transaction; contrast with **Write authority**.

### PLY-005: Prove torn-read safety across two connections

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-03. `playout-snapshot-consistency.test.ts` races
`ScheduleService.regenerate` on a second connection against the current-state
and following reads in both orderings, pausing the reader with `createBarrier`.
Splitting the snapshot into two transactions makes the paused cases fail.

**Goal**

Close the torn-read row plan 0004 handed to this plan.

**Scope**

- `playout/playout-snapshot-consistency.test.ts`: the reader runs
  `readPlayoutSnapshot` on a server database with a `deriveChannelState` reader
  and with a `selectFollowingPlayout` reader; the writer runs
  `ScheduleService.regenerate` on a second connection from
  `openTestDatabase(dataDirectory)` over a `createTemporaryDirectory()`
  directory, with distinct `sequentialIds` prefixes per side.

**Out of scope**

- Regeneration-versus-transition ordering, which SIG-013 owns.

**Blocking dependencies**

- PLY-003 and PLY-004.

**Implementation notes**

- Regeneration with an unchanged block restores progress, so new entries carry
  the same media and titles; assert on `scheduleEntryId` together with
  `scheduleRevision`.
- The following read uses the airing entry as its cursor, which regeneration
  keeps, so both orderings return `selected` with comparable items.
- Reader and writer use separate connections; Kysely's per-instance mutex
  would otherwise serialize them and hide the race.

**Verification**

- Reader paused in `afterRevisionRead`; writer regenerates and commits; reader
  resumes and returns the old revision with the old `nextItem` and following
  entry IDs.
- Writer commits first; reader returns the new revision with the new IDs.
- Both orderings run for the current-state read and the following read.
- No test sleeps; each completes deterministically.

**Docs impact**

- None.

## Phase 4: API

### PLY-006: Serve current channel state through PlayoutService and `GET /channels/:id/now`

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-03. `PlayoutService` serves `getCurrent`, `getFollowing`,
and `getScheduleRevision` with the one-ensure, one-retry coverage policy, and
`GET /channels/:id/now` maps its results. Unlike the note below,
`PlayoutService` takes no clock of its own: it reads `ScheduleService.now()`,
so playout and coverage always share one clock.

**Goal**

Deliver one vertical slice from snapshot through retry to the HTTP response,
and the service surface SIG-012 maps.

**Scope**

- `playout/playout-service.ts`: `PlayoutService` with
  `getCurrent(channelId, at, log)` and
  `getFollowing(channelId, afterScheduleEntryId, count, log)`, each returning
  the kraziBrain value or `not_found`, `disabled`, `through_out_of_range`, or
  `unavailable`; and `getScheduleRevision(channelId)`, returning a number.
- The retry in Resolved Implementation Policies.
- `playout/playout-routes.ts`: `GET /channels/:id/now?at=` with the `/now`
  shape and error mapping.
- Wire `PlayoutService` into `ServerDependencies` in `app.ts`, `index.ts`, and
  `testing/test-environment.ts`.

**Out of scope**

- `/playout` (PLY-007) and the signal port mapping (SIG-012).

**Blocking dependencies**

- PLY-004.

**Implementation notes**

- `PlayoutService` takes `db`, `now`, `Pick<ScheduleService, "ensureCoverage">`,
  and the snapshot hook option for tests.
- `getFollowing` passes no `through`; `getCurrent` passes `at`.
- `getScheduleRevision` is one `loadScheduleState` query, already atomic,
  returning `0` for a channel with no state, including an unknown one. Nothing
  in `packages/signal` calls it today.
- `startTestServer` builds the default `PlayoutService` from the final,
  possibly overridden `ScheduleService` and clock, so overriding `schedules`
  alone keeps them consistent.
- The route's mapping is its own: `PlayoutService` results differ from
  `EnsureCoverageResult`, so `sendCoverageFailure` stays private to the
  schedule routes. Both use `sendChannelNotFound` and `sendApiError`.

**Verification**

- `/now` on a covered channel returns the current item with `offsetMs` and
  `nextItem`; `?at=` evaluates at that instant deterministically.
- A channel short of its horizon gets coverage, then answers, and the revision
  matches the generated schedule.
- An unschedulable channel with no entries returns `schedule_gap` with
  revision `0`; one with entries still airing returns its current item.
- Missing media returns `media_unavailable` with the entry ID and leaves the
  schedule untouched.
- Disabled returns `409`, unknown returns `404`, and a bad or too-distant `at`
  returns `400`.
- With a writer held by `holdWriteAuthority`, a channel short of its horizon
  returns `503` with `retryable: true`, and a covered channel still returns
  `200`, proving covered reads never take write authority.
- With an `ensureCoverage` stub that returns `covered` without writing, the
  second snapshot is still short and the service returns `unavailable`.
- Responses never contain `mediaPath` or `hasAudio`.

**Docs impact**

- None.

### PLY-007: Expose bounded playout windows at `GET /channels/:id/playout`

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-03. `PlayoutService.getTimeline` builds the window's
playout timeline from one snapshot, and `GET /channels/:id/playout` serves it
with `/now`'s error mapping. Both window routes now share
`windowQuery(SCHEDULE_REQUEST_LIMIT_MS)` from `http/request-schemas.ts`.
Unlike the note below, `getTimeline` ensures coverage through `end`, so a
window past the horizon is never silently partial; an `end` past the request
limit returns `400`. `/schedule` is unchanged.

**Goal**

Return the playout timeline for a bounded window from one snapshot.

**Scope**

- `PlayoutService.getTimeline(channelId, start, end, log)` using the window
  query and `buildPlayoutTimeline`.
- `GET /channels/:id/playout?start&end` with the `/playout` shape and the same
  error mapping as `/now`.
- Add a `windowQuery(maxWindowMs)` factory to `http/request-schemas.ts`; both
  the schedule and playout routes call it with `SCHEDULE_REQUEST_LIMIT_MS`, so
  `http/` never imports a domain.

**Out of scope**

- Pagination.

**Blocking dependencies**

- PLY-006.

**Implementation notes**

- `getTimeline` passes no `through`, matching `/schedule`.

**Verification**

- Overlapping windows return identical items in the overlap.
- Unplayable entries are omitted, and the same window's `/schedule` still lists
  them.
- An unschedulable channel with no entries returns `200` with no items.
- A reversed window, a window over 7 days, or a non-UTC instant returns `400`;
  the existing schedule route tests stay green after the schema change.

**Docs impact**

- None.

## Phase 5: Acceptance

### PLY-008: Close executable acceptance and hand off

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-03. `playout/playout-acceptance.test.ts` drives `/now`
and `/playout` over HTTP through a mid-program join, a boundary, a mid-airing
regeneration, missing media, a restart, a disabled channel, and block removal.
Spec 0005 is `Implemented`; the worker-side rows stay with SIG-012 and SIG-013,
as listed under Hand-off.

**Goal**

Prove every spec 0005 criterion this plan owns against the real composition,
and record the hand-offs.

**Scope**

- `playout/playout-acceptance.test.ts` seeds the catalog through
  `startTestServer({ seed })`, as `schedule-acceptance.test.ts` does, with
  `ScheduleService` and the default `PlayoutService` on one manual clock. Over
  HTTP it creates a collection, a channel, and a block; joins mid-program;
  crosses a boundary; regenerates mid-airing; marks an item `missing` through
  the returned `db`; restarts on the same data directory; disables the
  channel; and removes the block.
- After regenerating mid-airing, assert the current item holds, the revision
  increments, and `nextItem.scheduleEntryId` is the new successor.
- After restarting, assert identical `/now` and `/playout` answers.
- Assert responses carry no `mediaPath`, `hasAudio`, provider, FFmpeg, or URL
  fields, and that no migration adds a playout or channel-state table.
- Mark spec 0005 `Implemented`. As with spec 0004, the worker-side rows stay
  handed off to plan 0006 and are listed below.

**Out of scope**

- The rows assigned to SIG-012 and SIG-013 (see Hand-off).

**Blocking dependencies**

- PLY-001 through PLY-007.

**Verification**

- Every traceability row below has a passing test, except the rows assigned to
  plan 0006. kraziBrain's dependency rule stays guarded by
  `packages/krazi-brain/src/index.test.ts`.

**Docs impact**

- Update the spec 0005 status line.

## Risk Register

| #   | Risk                                                              | Mitigation                                                                                                      | Tickets          |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| 1   | A snapshot query falls back to the root handle                    | `readPlayoutSnapshot` takes `Pick<Kysely, "transaction">` and passes only `trx`; review; a fallback hangs tests | PLY-004          |
| 2   | Torn-read test passes without exercising the race                 | Separate connections; assertions on entry IDs and revision; both orderings for current and following reads      | PLY-005          |
| 3   | Retry recomputes a later target and returns a spurious 503        | The second snapshot checks the first snapshot's `target`; one retry, then `503`                                 | PLY-004, PLY-006 |
| 4   | Reads take write authority to extend the horizon                  | Same cost `GET /schedule` pays today; chunked ensures keep each hold short; covered reads proven lock-free      | PLY-006          |
| 5   | Media re-probed shorter than its airtime                          | An exhausted offset gives `media_unavailable`; SIG-012 limits play duration and owns the early-end remainder    | PLY-002, SIG-012 |
| 6   | Following-item gaps stop a worker at a boundary                   | Accepted MVP behavior recorded in spec 0005; filler work supplies replacements later                            | PLY-001, PLY-003 |
| 7   | Ownership drifts back into SIG-012                                | PLY-001 edits plan 0006 before code; gates G1 and G3                                                            | PLY-001          |
| 8   | Playout and schedule routes differ for disabled or empty channels | Deliberate, documented in spec 0005, and tested                                                                 | PLY-001, PLY-006 |

## Hand-off

| Consumer              | Relies on                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SIG-012               | `PlayoutService.getCurrent`, `getFollowing`, and `getScheduleRevision`, mapped as below; `ChannelRepository.findById` for authorization. The adapter binds `server.log`, because the signal ports take no logger. Owns the `playout-projection.ts` clamp, including what a session does when media shorter than its airtime ends before the boundary. |
| SIG-013               | `loadScheduleState` and the covering query in `playout/playout-repository.ts`, run inside `runImmediateTransaction`. Owns the regeneration-versus-transition ordering rows.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| SIG-014               | Channel state's `schedule_gap` and `media_unavailable` reasons, surfaced through SIG-012, so the stream route fails before sending bytes.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Spec 0008 (Web Admin) | `GET /channels/:id/now` and `GET /channels/:id/playout` for debugging and admin screens.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

SIG-012 maps `PlayoutService` results onto the signal ports:

| `PlayoutService` result            | SIG-012 returns or throws                                                             |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Channel state `current`            | `CurrentPlayoutResult` `current`, with `offsetMs` as `mediaOffsetMs`                  |
| Channel state `no_current`         | `CurrentPlayoutResult` `no_current` with the same reason, revision, and entry ID      |
| Following `selected`/`stale_entry` | `FollowingPlayoutResult` with the same status, revision, and items                    |
| `not_found`                        | Throw `SignalError` `channel_not_found`                                               |
| `disabled`                         | Throw `SignalError` `channel_disabled`                                                |
| `unavailable`                      | Throw `SignalError` `playout_unavailable`; the worker fails and the next tune retries |
| `through_out_of_range`             | Programming error; ports never pass `at` beyond now                                   |
